sanskrit: yās te prācīḥ pradiśo yā udīcīr yās te bhūme adharād yāś ca paścāt | syonās tā mahyaṃ carate bhavantu mā ni paptaṃ bhuvane śiśriyāṇe ||
english: O Earth, may your eastern directions, your northern ones, those below you and those behind — may they all be pleasant for me as I travel; may I not fall in the world wherein I take my dwelling.

sanskrit: mā mā paścān mā purastān nudiṣṭhāḥ svasti bhūme me kṛṇu varīyo yāvayā vadhan mā vidan paripanthinaḥ ||
english: Push me not from behind, push me not from the front — O Earth, grant me well-being and breadth; drive away slaughter; let those who lie in ambush not find me.

sanskrit: yāvat te 'bhi vipaśyāmi bhūme sūryeṇa medinā | tāvan me cakṣur mā meṣṭa- -uttarām uttarāṃ samām ||
english: As far as I look upon you, O Earth, with the shining sun, so long may my sight not be extinguished — year after year, ever higher.

sanskrit: yat te bhūme vikhanāmy oṣaṃ tad api rohatu | mā te marma vimṛgvari mā te hṛdayam arpipam ||
english: Whatever I dig from you, O Earth, as a medicinal herb — may that grow back again; may I not pierce your vital parts, O one whom many search; may I not wound your heart.

sanskrit: yac chayānaḥ paryāvarte dakṣiṇaṃ savyam abhi bhūme pārśvam | uttānās tvā pratīcīṃ pṛṣṭyā yad abhiśemahe mā hiṃsīs tatra no bhūme sarvasya pratiśīvari ||
english: When lying down I turn upon my right or my left side, O Earth; when we stretch out on our backs, lying facing you with our spines — do not harm us then, O Earth, you who bestow healing on all things.

sanskrit: grīṣmas te bhūme varṣāṇi śarad dhemantaḥ śiśiro vasantaḥ | ṛtavas te vihitā hāyanā ahorātre pṛthivī no duhātām ||
english: Summer is yours, O Earth, and the rains, autumn, early winter, the cold season, and spring — your seasons are ordained year by year; may Earth with day and night yield nourishment to us.

sanskrit: yāpa sarpaṃ nudamānā vimṛgvarī yasyām āsann agnayo apsv antaḥ | parā dasyūn dadatī devapīyūn indraṃ vṛṇānā pṛthivī na vṛtraṃ śakrāya dadhre vṛṣabhāya vṛṣṇe | sa no bhūmer ā diśatu yad dhanaṃ kāmayāmahe ||
english: She who drives away the serpent and searches out all things, in whom the fires dwell within the waters — she who drives off the Dasyus who scoff at the gods, Earth who chose Indra as Vṛtra did not choose him, bearing him up for the mighty, the virile bull — may he point us toward the wealth from the Earth that we desire.

sanskrit: bhago anu prayuṅktām indro yātu purogavaḥ | yasyāṃ sadohavirdhāne yūpo yasyāṃ nimīyate | brahmāṇo yasyām arcanti ṛgbhiḥ sāmnā yajurvidaḥ | yujyante yasyām ṛtvijaḥ somam indrāya pātave | sā no bhūmir dakṣiṇāyāṃ suśevā yajñe dadhātu sumanasyamānā ||
english: May Bhaga set things in motion; may Indra go as the leader of the herd; she upon whom stand the sacrificial hall and the offering-shed, upon whom the post is fixed, upon whom the brahmins chant with Ṛgvedic hymns, those who know the Yajurveda with Sāman, upon whom the ritual priests are yoked to press soma for Indra to drink — may that Earth, well-disposed, place us graciously on the southern side at the sacrifice.

sanskrit: yasyāṃ pūrve bhūtakṛta ṛṣayo gā udānṛcuḥ | sapta satreṇa vedhaso yajñena tapasā saha | sā naḥ paśūn viśvarūpān dadhātu dīrghaṃ ma āyuḥ savitā kṛṇotu ||
english: She upon whom the ancient world-making seers sang forth the cows, the seven wise ones together through sacrifice, ascetic rite, and the extended soma session — may she bestow on us cattle of every kind; may Savitṛ grant me long life.

sanskrit: yasyām annaṃ vrīhiyavau yatremāḥ pañca kṛṣṭayaḥ | bhūmyai parjanyapatnyai namo 'stu varṣam edhate ||
english: She upon whom are food, rice, and barley, upon whom these five peoples dwell — to Earth, whose lord is Parjanya, let there be homage; let rain increase.

sanskrit: yasyāṃ gāyanti nṛtyanti janā martyā vailavāḥ | yujyante yasyām ākrando yasyāṃ vadati dundubhiḥ | sā no bhūmiḥ pra ṇudatāṃ sapatnān yo no dveṣṭy adharaṃ taṃ kṛṇotu ||
english: She upon whom mortals, the people of the village settlements, sing and dance; upon whom the battle-cry is raised, upon whom the war-drum sounds — may that Earth drive away our rivals; may she bring low the one who hates us.

sanskrit: yasyāṃ puro devakṛtāḥ kṣetre yasyāṃ vikurvate | prajāpatiḥ pṛthivīṃ viśvagarbhām āśāmāśāṃ raṇyāṃ naḥ kṛṇotu ||
english: She upon whom the divine-built cities stand, upon whose field they display their power — may Prajāpati make this Earth, who bears all creatures in her womb, delightful for us in every direction.

sanskrit: janaṃ bibhratī bahudhā vivācasaṃ nānādharmāṇaṃ pṛthivī yathaukasam | sahasraṃ dhārā draviṇasya no duhāṃ dhruveva dhenur anapasphurantī ||
english: Earth bearing in many ways a people of diverse speech and diverse customs, each as if at home — like a steady cow that does not kick, may she yield us a thousand streams of wealth.

sanskrit: yas te sarpo vṛścikas tṛṣṭadaṃśmā hemantajabdho bhṛmalo guhā śaye | krimir ilmaṃ pṛthivi prāvṛṣi yad ejati tan naḥ sarpan mopa sṛpad yac chivaṃ tena no mṛḍa ||
english: Whatever serpent, scorpion, sharp-fanged, frost-roused, buzzing worm lies in a crevice — the worm that stirs in the swampy ground in the rainy season, O Earth — may that crawler not creep upon us; and whatever is auspicious in it, with that be gracious to us.

sanskrit: ye te panthāno bahudhā janāyanā rathasya vartman manasaś ca yātave | yebhiś caranty ubhaye bhadrapāpās taṃ panthāṃ jayemānamitram ataskaram ||
english: Your roads that lead people in many directions, the track of the chariot, and the paths along which the mind travels — upon which both the good and the wicked walk — may we conquer on that path, free from foes, free from thieves.

sanskrit: mandaṃ (⟨ malvaṃ?) bibhratī gurubhṛd bhadrapāpasya nidhanaṃ titikṣuḥ | sūkareṇa pṛthivī saṃvidānā varāhāya vi jihīte mṛgāya ||
english: Bearing the sluggish (or the soft?), heavy-bearing, enduring the dissolution of both good and evil — Earth, in accord with the boar, opens herself wide for the wild boar.

sanskrit: ye ta āranyāḥ paśavo mṛgā vane hitāḥ siṃhā vyāghrāḥ puruṣādaś caranti | ulaṃ vṛkaṃ pṛthivi ducchunām ita ṛkṣīkāṃ rakṣo apa badhāsmat ||
english: Your forest-dwelling animals, the beasts set loose in the woods, lions and tigers that roam man-eating — O Earth, drive away from here the hyena, the wolf, the evil omen, the she-bear, and the demon.

sanskrit: ye gandharvāpsaraso ye carāyāḥ kimīdinaḥ | piśācān sarvā rakṣāṃsi tān asmad bhūme yāvaya ||
english: Gandharvas and Apsarases, those who wander about, the kimīdins — Piśācas, all the Rākṣasas — O Earth, drive all of them away from us.

sanskrit: yāṃ dvipādaḥ pakṣiṇaḥ saṃpatanti haṃsāḥ suparṇāḥ śakunā vayāṃsi | yasyāṃ vāta īyate mātariśvā rajāṃsi kṛṇvaṃś cyāvayaṃś ca vṛkṣān | vātasya pravām upavām anu vāty arcir yasyāṃ kṛṣṇam aruṇaṃ ca saṃbhṛte ahorātre vihite bhūmyām adhi ||
english: She to whom winged two-footed creatures fly — swans, eagles, birds, and fowl; upon whom the wind, Mātariśvan, moves, raising dust-clouds and shaking the trees; the flame that blows along the forward and the inward current of the wind — she upon whom the black and the red are gathered together, upon whom day and night are ordained, spread out over the Earth.

sanskrit: varṣeṇa bhūmiḥ pṛthivī vṛtāvṛtā | sā no dadhātu bhadrayā priye dhāmanidhāmani ||
english: Earth, enveloped and re-enveloped by the rain — may she sustain us with blessing in each beloved dwelling-place and resting-place.

sanskrit: dyauś ca ma idaṃ pṛthivī ca- -antarikṣaṃ ca me vyacaḥ | agniḥ sūrya āpo medhāṃ viśve devāś ca saṃ dadhuḥ ||
english: Sky and Earth — this expanse — and the midspace have given me room; Fire, the Sun, the Waters, and all the gods together have bestowed wisdom upon me.

sanskrit: aham asmi sahamāna uttaro nāma bhūmyām | abhisāḍ asmi viśvāṣāḍ āśāmāśāṃ viṣāsahiḥ ||
english: I am the prevailing one, named the Higher, here on Earth; I am the overpowerer, the all-conqueror, ever victorious in every direction.

sanskrit: yad ado devi prathamānā purastād devaiḥ sṛṣṭā vyasarpo mahitvam | ā tvā subhūtam aviśat tadānīm akalpayathāḥ pradiśaś catasraḥ ||
english: O goddess, when you first spread out there in front, sent forth by the gods, you pervaded greatness — well-being entered into you at that very moment; you arranged the four directions.

sanskrit: ye grāmā yāny araṇyāni yāḥ sabhā adhi bhūmyām | teṣv ahaṃ devi pṛthivy udyāsaṃ madhumad vacaḥ ||
english: In the villages, in the wildernesses, in the assembly halls that are upon the Earth — among them, O goddess Earth, may I rise up with honey-sweet speech.

sanskrit: yad vadāni madhumat tad vadāni yad īkṣe ṣutadyaḥ punantu mā | tviṣīmān asmi jūtimān yān hanmi dodhataḥ ||
english: What I speak, may I speak it sweetly; what I see, may the soma-pressers purify me; I am lustrous, I am impelled — those whom I strike down are the agitators.

sanskrit: aśva iva rajo duduhe vi taṃ janaṃ ya ākṣiyan pṛthivīm ād ajāyata | madrā pari bhuvanasya gopā vanaspatīnāṃ gṛbhir oṣadhīnām ||
english: Like a horse she has milked the dust — she scattered that people who oppressed the Earth when she was born; the gracious one, guardian of the world, embracing the forest trees and the herbs.

sanskrit: śantivā surabhiḥ syonā kīlālodhnī payasvatī | bhūmir no adhi bravītu pṛthivī payasā saha ||
english: Peaceful, fragrant, pleasant, her udder filled with sweet drink, milk-laden — may Earth speak over us; may the Earth speak together with her milk.

sanskrit: bhūmi mātar ni dhehi mā bhadrayā supratiṣṭhitam | saṃvidānā divā tvaṃ śriyāṃ mā dhehi bhūtyām ||
english: O Mother Earth, set me down well-established in blessing; you who are in accord with Heaven — set me in splendor, in prosperity.

sanskrit: yām anvaicchad dhaviṣā viśvakarmā yasyām āsann agnayo 'psv antaḥ | bhujiṣyaṃ pātraṃ nihitaṃ guhā- -āsīd āvir bhogair abhavan mātṛmadbhiḥ ||
english: She whom Viśvakarmā sought out with an oblation, in whom the fires dwell within the waters — the vessel of enjoyment was laid hidden in a secret place; it became manifest with its riches, possessed of motherly powers.

sanskrit: tvam asy āvapanī janānām aditiḥ kāmadughā viśvarūpā | yat ta ūnaṃ tat ta ā pūrayāti prajāpatiḥ prajābhiḥ saṃvidānaḥ ||
english: You are the scattering-ground of peoples, Aditi, yielding all desires, of all forms; whatever is deficient in you, Prajāpati, in accord with his creatures, fills that up for you.
